title: Integral ring-object constructibility and the completed category
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Z$ be a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible: $Z$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], so it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, a finite bound on chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring. Put $B_Z=p_Z^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Identify it with $\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/\varpi^n)_Z$ by the canonical coefficient-limit map [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. In the ordinary category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_Z))$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], for every $K$ the following conditions are equivalent:

(i) $K$ is bounded constructible in the general ring-object sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]: its cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and, after a finite constructible locally closed stratification, each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally a cokernel of a finite matrix over $B_Z$.

(ii) $K$ belongs to the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: it is derived $\varpi$-complete, and its derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_Z}(A/\varpi^n)_Z$ have compatible étale-origin representatives with classical constructible cohomology, all in a single cohomological interval independent of $n$.

(iii) $K$ is bounded and its cohomology sheaves, after finite stratification, are pro-étale locally $B_V\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; here $A$ and $P$ in this tensor denote constant sheaves. The stratifications in (i) and (iii) may differ. Torsion cohomology is allowed, and no completeness hypothesis is imposed in (i).

proof.text: Use the proved integralLfpConstantModelComparison. Its WithAbs coefficient model is transported first to the embedded valuation ring by the proved integralCoefficientIso helper of IntegralConstantModelHeartClosure, and then to DerivedNakayama.integerRing by the proved integerRingSheafIso helper of IntegralCoefficientExtComparison. The composite is an actual ring isomorphism. Restriction of scalars preserves and reflects both general stratified local finite presentation and finite constant local models; use its identity round trip to obtain the two predicates on the original module M.

Apply the preceding module equivalence to every cohomology sheaf. Both bounded predicates retain precisely the same standard t-structure boundedness, so conjunction and universal quantifier congruence give (i) iff (iii) without completing K.

Let S be integralSectionFunctor and let R be restriction along integralDetailedCoefficientComparison.hom. These are additive exact faithful functors. Standard derived exact-functor cohomology isomorphisms identify R(S(H^q K)) with H^q(D(R)(D(S)(K))). The new heart-level scalar-model comparison and invariance under this cohomology isomorphism identify finite constant models degreewise with IsIntegralStratifiedFinitelyPresented. Faithful exact functors preserve and reflect boundedness; replace bounds a,b by min(a,b),b to meet the completed predicate convention. Thus (iii) is IsIntegralBoundedConstructibleCohomology of the transported original K.

Apply the two proved equivalences of integralStratifiedPerfectCharacterization on Z to identify this cohomological predicate with PbcIsBoundedConstructibleComplete. Apply its integralStratifiedPerfectDetailed clause at the canonical integralSectionDerivedEquivalence image of K. These functors are definitionally the two derived exact functors used above. Transitivity gives (iii) iff (ii), and composing with step 2 gives the requested conjunction. The Noetherian, finite-dimensional and ell-invertible hypotheses are exactly those supplied in the theorem; no hypothesis is imposed on cover members.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q64-3096e87b9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item with every cited statement open. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from the landed base. There are 0 new nodes, and the split is an assembly of existing nodes. I found no cycle (the closure of the cited nodes does not contain the item) and no re-split note. (ii)<=>(iii) is lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization applied on Z (step 7). Its detailed-category clause supplies completeness, compatible étale witnesses and the uniform [r,s], which matches Bhatt-Scholze Prop. 6.8.11(3) with Def. 6.5.1 and 6.8.10. (i)=>(iii) works as follows. Step 2 shows the strata are Noetherian, finite-dimensional and qcqs with ℓ invertible; these facts are elementary from the three Noetherian leaves. On each stratum, lem-weil-pbc-integral-lfp-locally-free-resolution gives 0->F1->F0->P->0 with F_i locally finite free. F_i[0] is a perfect constant model, the SES triangle and cone closure put P[0] in the category, and the characterization's (iii) gives scalar models. lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement gives actual morphisms to the strata, and constant models pull back. (iii)=>(i) uses det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model (finite constant model => lfp). The coefficients B_Z = lim (A/ϖ^n)_Z are the same ring in all three cited frameworks via sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x and the Cartesian clause. Edge cases checked: Z empty and K=0 are trivial; over Spec of a separably closed field an lfp module is constant; B[1/ϖ] is excluded from (ii); (A/ϖ^r)_Z has uniform reduction amplitude [-1,0]. I accept the declared tool_uses because the unit route via sk-lem-integral-models needs finite type over a field. No duplicate exists in the DAG and the item cites no SGA. Advisory only: step 5 could say in one clause that locally closed strata of the Noetherian Z are constructible.
